sentences.text: Shri Saranjit Singh Chawla, learned counsel for the res  ORDER 1.

The appellant - claimant has filed this appeal under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 being aggrieved by award dated 10.08.2024 passed in Claim Case bearing No. 451/2021 by Member of Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District-Indore (M.P.) whereby a total compensation amount of Rs.8,15,386/- has been awarded in favour of the claimant.
2.
The present appeal is filed seeking enhancement in compensation amount amount up to Rs.1,00,000/- alongwith interest @ 6%.
3. In short, the facts of the case are that on 30.06.2020 at about 11:00 pm, the appellant was going towards Borkheda on his motorcycle.

When he reached in front of Gujrati Dhaba, at the same time,
respondent No. 2 has dashed him by Eisher bearing registration No. MP09 GE 9328, thereby the appellant fell down and sustained various severe injuries.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:12191 2 MA-9853-2024 4.

The Tribunal while awarding the amount of compensation has considered the entire evidence placed on record and after recording evidence Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs.8,15,386/- in the following heads :-

sentences.text: This appeal has been filed on the ground that the Learned Member of the Tribunal has wrongly adjudicated the income of the appellant.
The Tribunal has also erred in holding that the appellant has suffered only 25% permanent disability and passed award on this head only Rs.8,15,386/-.
The appellant was young and was earning for his livelihood by doing labour work.
Due to the accident he has suffered several severe injuries in different parts of body, which made him incapable for doing physical work.

The learned Tribunal has decided the claim of the appellant without minutely going through the documents exhibited which includes history of treatment NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:12191 3 MA-9853-2024 the appellant from the date of accident.
The interest of 6% is also on very low as per settled law on this point.
The income of the appellant is calculated by the Tribunal as Rs. 8,275/- per month which is also on the lower side.
On these grounds, it is prayed for enhancement of compensation.

6. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent has opposed the submissions made by counsel for the appellant and submitted that the Tribunal has not committed any error and has rightly passed the award in favour of the appellant.
Hence, prayer for enhancement of compensation be rejected.
7. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, I find substance in the arguments advanced by the counsel for the appellant.
So far as the quantum of compensation awarded by the Claims Tribunal is concerned, looking to the income as well as age, compensation awarded by the Tribunal can be enhanced to some extent.

Hemraj vs Oriental Insurance Company Limited on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177953086/
2 8.

sentences.text: On perusal of medical documents produced on behalf of appellant/claimant before the Claims Tribunal and looking to the injuries sustained by the appellant, especially the permanent disability certificate produced by doctor concerned, this Court thinks it appropriate to assume income of Rs.8,950/- per month in place of Rs.8,275/- per month, for a year, it comes to Rs.1,07,400/- and alongwith 40% future prospects, it becomes Rs.1,50,360/- per year.

Accordingly, the compensation is recalculated as under:
 Heads Amount  Income Assessed Rs.1,07,400/
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:12191 4 MA-9853-2024 (minimum wages for unskilled labour (8950X12) as per labour commissioner office) Future prospect 40% Rs.42,963/-
 Net Income Rs.1,
 Loss of income due to injuries  25% of (1,50,360X18=27,06,480/-) Rs.6  Medical Expenses Rs.29  Loss of income during lay off  (03 months) (6713X3 months) (8950-25%) Rs..2  Transportation + Special diet Rs.12,
 Loss of life expectancy Rs.50  Pain & suffering Rs.80
TOTAL Rs.8,

9 . Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs. 8,76,898/- as against the Award of the Claims Tribunal of Rs.8,15,386/- Accordingly, the appellant/claimant is entitled to an additional sum of Rs.52,512/- over and above the amount, which has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
10. In the result, this miscellaneous appeal is partly allowed, by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.52,512/-.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest as fixed by the learned Claims Tribunal from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.

The said amount be paid Hemraj vs Oriental Insurance Company Limited on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177953086/
3 within a period of three months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
